title: Towards Secure AI How far can international standards take us?
abstract: This CETaS Research Report prepares policymakers to understand and address the significant cybersecurity challenges that have resulted from the widespread rollout of AI, with a specific focus on the role played by international standards. Our findings indicate that many of the challenges associated with securing AI systems are not new and can be resolved by updating existing cybersecurity standards. However, several challenges are new and evolving rapidly, such as those relating to the security of AI supply chains and new threats which have emerged in the context of generative AI. Standards development organisations (SDOs) have begun to introduce international standards which help protect AI systems from attack, but these standards are at a nascent stage. We recommend governments redouble their efforts to support SDOs and to ensure crucial international standards are made available and accessible to those who need to implement them. We also recommend further investment in related research to advance understandings of adversarial AI, ensuring that future international standards don’t just focus on identifying vulnerabilities, but instead offer robust and specific mitigation strategies.

title: pfoqcompiler: Efficient Compilation of Quantum Control in Recursive First-Order Quantum Programs
abstract: This is an artifact for the paper "pfoqcompiler: Efficient Compilation of Quantum Control in Recursive First-Order Quantum Programs". pfoqcompiler is a compiler for First-Order Quantum (FOQ) programs that outputs Qiskit circuits, implementing the 'anchoring and merging' compilation technique and including static analysis tools that ensure complexity bounds on circuit size and depth.

title: Quantum Information Cryptography: Adaptive Key Generation
abstract: Quantum information cryptography (QIC) is rapidly emerging as a crucial component of modern cybersecurity, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to secure communication. This paper presents a novel quantum key generation (QKD) algorithm, "Adaptive Quantum Key Generation," designed to address limitations of existing approaches by exploiting quantum entanglement's self-adjusting nature. The core mechanism centers around creating entangled states that exhibit dynamic correlations, allowing for precise key generation and enhanced security. We detail the algorithm's architecture, explain the underlying quantum principles, and present preliminary results demonstrating significant improvements in key generation rate and security against known attacks. This work explores the potential of this adaptive approach to revolutionize QIC, offering a pathway towards robust and adaptable cryptographic systems.

title: Formal Verification of Old-Age Pension Eligibility (Decreto-Lei n.º 187/2007)
abstract: A faithful-by-construction formalization of the old-age pension eligibility rules of the Portuguese General Social Security Regime (Decreto-Lei n.º 187/2007, original 2007 wording), specified in First-Order Logic, implemented in Catala, and machine-verified in Lean 4 by an adequacy theorem relating the executable definition to the logical specification for every beneficiary. Part of doctoral research on formal verification of old-age and invalidity pensions within the Rules as Code paradigm. Source code is licensed under Apache-2.0; the documentation and formalization text under CC BY 4.0.

title: Memory Quantum Cipher Identification Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel Memory Quantum Cipher Identification Algorithm (MQCA) designed to efficiently identify and track quantum states, offering enhanced security for quantum computing. The MQCA leverages the unique properties of quantum variables to construct an intelligent detection algorithm. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting quantum entanglement to establish a robust and efficient tracking system for hidden information within quantum states. This approach promises to significantly improve the detection and analysis of quantum states, thereby bolstering the security of quantum computations. The algorithm's design incorporates a refined quantum state analysis framework, resulting in improved accuracy and speed compared to existing methods. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of quantum cryptography and offers a practical framework for secure quantum communication.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Graph-Based Semantic Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning leveraging graph-based semantic networks. The core idea is to bridge the gap between neural networks, known for their pattern recognition capabilities, and symbolic reasoning systems, prized for their logical deduction abilities. We introduce a system where a neural network learns to predict relationships within a structured semantic network, represented as a graph. These predictions dynamically guide the application of symbolic inference rules, and conversely, the results of symbolic inference inform the neural network's learning. This creates a continuous feedback loop, fostering robust and explainable AI. The system's architecture allows for both inductive and deductive reasoning, capitalizing on the strengths of both paradigms. The key innovation lies in the tightly integrated feedback mechanism and the use of a graph-based semantic network to provide a flexible and interpretable knowledge representation. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework and outline future research directions.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks with Adaptive Learning Rate Schedules Based on Prediction Error
abstract: This paper presents a novel architecture for neural networks designed to mitigate the challenges associated with traditional training methods, specifically the need for meticulous tuning of learning rate schedules. The proposed network, termed a Self-Correcting Neural Network (SCNN), incorporates a feedback mechanism that dynamically adjusts the learning rate of individual weights based on the observed prediction error. This adaptive learning rate schedule is intrinsically linked to the contribution of each weight to the overall error, fostering a more robust and efficient training process. The core claim of this work is that such an architecture can achieve faster convergence and improved performance compared to conventional neural network training paradigms. We detail the architecture and the associated mathematical formulation, focusing on the predictive error calculation and the weight adaptation process. The key innovation lies in the automated, data-driven adjustment of learning rates, eliminating the need for manual hyperparameter optimization, and demonstrating a potentially significant advantage in complex learning scenarios.

title: Adaptive Quantum Computing Simulations for Machine Learning
abstract: The simulation of quantum computers presents a formidable challenge due to the exponential growth in computational cost with the number of qubits. Current simulation methods often struggle to scale to even moderately sized quantum systems, severely limiting their applicability for machine learning applications. This paper introduces an adaptive simulation strategy designed to mitigate this issue. The core idea revolves around dynamically adjusting the simulation complexity—the level of detail—based on the demands of the underlying machine learning task. We propose a hierarchical simulation approach, where a coarse-grained representation is utilized initially, and the simulation is progressively refined, or "zoomed in," only when specific regions or interactions become critical for the learning process. This strategy minimizes unnecessary computations, leading to a significant reduction in overall simulation time and resource requirements. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and the formulation of key equations governing the adaptive simulation process. The primary goal is to achieve a more efficient and practical approach to quantum computing simulations for machine learning, paving the way for the exploration of quantum algorithms within the machine learning domain.

title: Quantum-Induced Topological Phase Field Dynamics
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to induce topological phase field dynamics, a novel approach to generating complex and dynamically evolving phase field structures. We investigate a new algorithmic framework predicated on creating intricate entanglement patterns that fundamentally alter the behavior of topological phase fields. The core mechanism centers around utilizing entanglement to construct a dynamic and intricate network of quantum states, leading to the emergence of unique topological phases. This research aims to address limitations of existing techniques by providing a fundamentally new methodology for shaping phase field behavior. The paper outlines the proposed algorithm, its theoretical foundations, and preliminary experimental demonstrations illustrating its potential for generating novel phase field topologies.

title: Symbolic Regression with Learned Grammatical Structures
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its efficacy is often limited by the exponential growth of the search space, leading to the generation of overly complex and often uninterpretable models. This work proposes a novel approach to SR that addresses this challenge by integrating learned grammatical structures into the regression process. The core idea is to utilize a learned grammar to guide the search, favoring mathematical expressions that adhere to the learned structural patterns, thereby promoting conciseness and interpretability. We hypothesize that by incorporating this grammatical knowledge, the search space can be significantly reduced, leading to the discovery of more meaningful and readily understandable equations. This paper outlines the framework, presents the key components, and discusses the potential impact of this approach on the field of symbolic regression.

title: Formal Program Semantic Understanding (FPSU)
abstract: This paper introduces Formal Program Semantic Understanding (FPSU), a novel approach to program semantic understanding that leverages formal logic and automated reasoning. The core claim is to transform program semantic understanding into a formal logical inference problem, enabling rigorous verification and optimization through established formal methods. We propose a mechanism involving the construction of a program semantic ontology and its translation into formal logical expressions. These expressions are then subjected to verification using theorem provers or model checkers. This approach shifts the paradigm from treating program semantics as a black box to a verifiable, logical process, ultimately enhancing software reliability and understandability. We outline the key components of the FPSU framework and discuss its potential impact on software development and verification.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Accelerated Distributed Data Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed data verification leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to utilize entangled particles to establish instantaneous correlations between distributed data segments, thereby enabling rapid detection of data corruption or loss. Traditional distributed data verification methods are inherently limited by the speed of light and the need for classical communication, leading to significant latency. This work demonstrates how entanglement can potentially bypass these limitations, offering a pathway to dramatically accelerated verification times. We outline the key components of the system, including entangled state generation, distribution, and measurement protocols. The theoretical framework is presented, focusing on the mathematical underpinnings of the verification process. We explore scenarios where the verification speed surpasses classical methods, highlighting the potential of quantum entanglement for secure and efficient data validation in distributed systems. The proposed methodology provides a foundation for future research and development in quantum-enhanced distributed computing.

title: Non-Linear Geometry Topology: A Foundation for Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear geometry topology to revolutionize quantum computation. We investigate how leveraging quantum entanglement can enhance the computational precision of geometric operations, paving the way for algorithms exceeding the limitations of current quantum devices. The core concept centers around dynamically controlled "quantum topology fields" which act as fundamental parameters, facilitating complex geometric transformations and the generation of novel quantum states. This approach promises significant performance gains through enhanced computational speed and the ability to overcome the inherent bottlenecks of traditional quantum algorithms. The paper details the proposed mechanism, highlighting the importance of quantum entanglement in driving the computational process and ultimately showcasing the potential for a paradigm shift in quantum computation.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Network Design
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum entanglement network, the 'Dynamic Entanglement Lattice,' aiming to achieve exponential speedups in quantum computation through adaptive entanglement protocols. We propose a system of interconnected nodes, each capable of modulating entanglement strength based on a feedback loop, to optimize performance and resilience. The core mechanism centers around this dynamic lattice, offering a fundamentally different approach to quantum information processing compared to existing architectures. The research investigates the potential for exponential speedups and addresses critical limitations within current quantum computing paradigms. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this innovative network design.

abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning framework utilizing dynamic topology-based adjustments to enhance exploration and stability. Current reinforcement learning algorithms often struggle with complex, dynamically changing environments, limiting the potential for robust agent learning. Our work introduces a mechanism that allows the agent to dynamically modify the topology of its environment during training, thereby facilitating more efficient exploration and mitigating instability. The core principle is to create a self-adjusting network structure that adapts to the agent's learning process, offering a significant improvement over static approaches. We detail the proposed architecture, training methodology, and initial results demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in a simulated environment. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, focusing on scalability and generalization.

title: 基于自适应模型的迁移学习的动态特征选择
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for dynamic feature selection and adjustment within a transfer learning paradigm. Traditional approaches often rely on static feature selection, limiting the model's ability to adapt to the intricacies of the input data. This work proposes a system that dynamically selects and adjusts model features based on the characteristics of the input data, leading to improved model generalization and performance. The proposed method utilizes a self-adaptive model to iteratively refine feature representations, enhancing the model's robustness and predictive power. The core of the innovation lies in the framework's ability to dynamically adjust feature importance based on the data's evolution, addressing a significant limitation of standard transfer learning techniques. We evaluate the framework's efficacy on a diverse dataset, demonstrating a substantial improvement in both accuracy and robustness compared to baseline models.

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Quantum Computation Topology Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computation topology optimization based on dynamic topology. Traditional topology optimization methods often require manual design, which is challenging for complex quantum computing environments. Our method leverages dynamic topology to automatically optimize the quantum computation's topology, leading to improved computational efficiency and stability. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts the quantum circuit's topology during the optimization process, resulting in a more robust and efficient solution. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the proposed algorithm and its implementation, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing quantum circuits for specific scenarios. The core of the method lies in the utilization of self-similarity properties within the topological landscape, allowing for a streamlined and adaptive optimization process. We discuss the challenges and benefits of this approach, highlighting its potential to advance quantum computation.

title: Title: Topological Quantum Entanglement for Information Encoding
abstract: Abstract: Topological quantum entanglement (TQE) represents a paradigm shift in quantum information processing, offering the potential for robust and scalable entanglement across macroscopic distances. This paper explores the development of a novel topological quantum state, tentatively termed "Dynamically Evolving Topological Structure" (DETS), designed to facilitate long-lasting and controllable entanglement. We delve into the underlying principles of phase transitions and string theory, proposing a dynamic structure that self-assembles into a highly stable entanglement network. This work addresses the limitations of current qubit entanglement by leveraging topological properties, offering a pathway towards secure communication and data storage surpassing existing capabilities.

title: Knowledge-guided adaptive educational support for traditional Chinese medicine using large language models and knowledge graphs: integrating Confucian educational principles
abstract: Introduction: The Confucian principle of "teaching students in accordance with their aptitude" remains challenging to implement at scale in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) education. We developed an Intelligent TCM Tutoring System integrating a large language model (LLM) with a domain-specific knowledge graph (KG) derived from the Golden Mirror of Medicine and evaluated its system performance and short-term educational outcomes. Methods: System outputs were rated by five TCM teachers. In a three-group pedagogical experiment, 125 student volunteers were randomly allocated to self-directed learning, LLM-assisted learning, or learning with the integrated system, and 102 questionnaires were included in the final analysis. Results: The integrated system received higher expert ratings than the LLM baseline without KG integration in instructional content generation, intelligent question answering, and automated test generation and grading. Students using the integrated system achieved significantly higher immediate post-test scores than both comparison groups and reported more favorable post-session learning experience ratings in relevant comparisons. Discussion: These findings provide preliminary evidence that an LLM-KG system can enhance immediate learning outcomes and learning experiences in this educational setting.

title: Integrating Knowledge Management and AI for optimizing customer experience
abstract: In today’s digital service landscape, organizations increasingly deploy Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies in the hope of delivering faster, more personalized, and seamless customer experiences. However, many firms continue to face challenges in translating AI capabilities into measurable improvements in customer satisfaction, largely because AI tools often operate without adequate support from structured Knowledge Management (KM) practices. When the knowledge base behind automated systems is fragmented or inconsistent, customers encounter variability in service quality, reduced trust, and limited personalization depth. This study investigates how AI-enabled service attributes supported by KM-related perceptions shape overall customer experience by analyzing empirical data from 300 customers who regularly engage with AI-driven service platforms. The dataset captures key experiential dimensions, including personalization, service speed, ease of use, trust in AI, and the perceived usefulness of knowledge support embedded in automated service responses. Using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, regression modelling, and ANOVA, the study finds that trust in AI systems and perceived KM usefulness exert the strongest influence on overall satisfaction, while other attributes such as personalization and ease of use demonstrate weaker predictive power. The results also reveal that customer satisfaction does not significantly differ across varying levels of AI interaction frequency, suggesting that qualitative aspects of AI-based interactions matter more than the volume of usage. Overall, the findings emphasize that optimal customer experience arises not from AI functionality alone, but from the quality, clarity, and reliability of the knowledge that informs AI outputs. The study provides empirical insights to guide organizations in strengthening KM foundations to support AI systems more effectively and enhance customer experience outcomes.

title: Внедрение цифрового анализатора потребностей клиента в сфере производства оконных и дверных систем
abstract: Целью работы является разработка модели внедрения ИИ- анализатора для привлечения потребности клиента, привлечения и удержания клиента доя заключения сделки. Были решены следующие задачи: - изучены существующие методы маркетинговых решений, виды стратегии продвижения, методы продвижения товаров и услуг; - выявлены основные проблемы, с которыми сталкивается компания в сфере производства оконных и дверных систем; - разработан единый механизм ИИ – анализатора; - проведен анализ экономической привлекательности модели. Предложенная модель демонстрирует высокую актуальность, так как затрагивает ключевые проблемы маркетинга и предлагает инновационное решение для конкретной отрасли, что позволяет существенно повысить рентабельность рекламных кампаний и сократить издержки привлечения клиентов. Источниками информации выступили данные зарубежной и отечественной научно-исследовательской литературы, официальных Интернет-ресурсов. Предложенная модель может быть применена как в оконно-дверной отрасли, так и в других сегментах бизнеса с учетом отраслевых особенностей.

title: Three-Photon and Hybrid Coherent-Fock Interference in a Two-Phase Six-Port Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
abstract: We present a unified theoretical analysis of three-photon quantum interference in a Six-Port Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (6p-MZI) constructed from two cascaded tritters, with two independent phase modulators placed between the tritter arms. We analytically derive the transfer matrix of the 6p-MZI and show how they organize into three symmetry classes, governed by the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) structure of the tritter and the conjugate relations. Furthermore, we analyze two input regimes: First, three indistinguishable single photons are injected into the tritter, and the output probability distributions $P_{[111]}$, $P_{[\{300\}]}$, and $P_{[\{210\}]}$ are derived as functions of the two relative phases $(ϕ_1, ϕ_2)$. At $ϕ_2 = 0$, the single-phase limit is recovered, which confirms 100\% visibility of the even-distribution fringe. Second, a hybrid coherent-Fock input $|α\rangle_1|α\rangle_2|1\rangle_3$ is analyzed via the density matrix formalism. The average photon number at each output port exhibits amplitude-dependent phase shifts. Our results establish the 6p-MZI as a programmable platform for tripartite quantum state manipulation and coherent amplitude sensing.

title: Projected Riemannian Gradient Descent for the Bures-Wasserstein Barycenter: Dimension-Independent Linear Convergence at Unit Step Size
abstract: The computation of the Bures-Wasserstein (BW) barycenter of an ensemble of positive definite matrices arises throughout machine learning, optimal transport, and quantum information. Riemannian gradient descent (RGD) at unit step size -- the fixed-point iteration used in practice -- converges rapidly, yet existing analyses present a dichotomy: unit-step guarantees carry worst-case exponential dependence on the dimension, while dimension-independent guarantees require small step sizes that forfeit the empirical speed. We resolve this dichotomy, not by improving the guarantees for unit-step RGD, but by proposing a Projected RGD algorithm that achieves dimension-independent linear convergence at unit step size. The achieved rate, $(1 - κ^{-3/2})$, where $κ$ is the condition number of the ensemble, also polynomially improves on the best small-step guarantee ($κ^{3/2}$ versus $κ^{5/2}$ iteration complexity). The crux is a novel Projection Lemma: clipping the eigenvalues of a positive matrix to an interval $[α, β]$ is the closed-form, non-expansive (1-Lipschitz) BW-metric projection onto the set $\{S : αI \leq S \leq βI\}$ -- a statement which, unlike its known one-sided counterpart, does not follow from convexity. The projection is moreover free: it reuses an eigendecomposition the next iteration must perform in any case, so the projected and unprojected iterations cost the same per step. The same analysis covers the invariant matrix projection problem of Brahmachari et al. (2025), whose fixed-point algorithm we identify as unit-step RGD on a totally geodesic submanifold, thereby extending the dimension-independent guarantee to that setting verbatim.

title: RAFT: A Real-World Few-Shot Text Classification Benchmark
abstract: Large pre-trained language models have shown promise for few-shot learning, completing text-based tasks given only a few task-specific examples. Will models soon solve classification tasks that have so far been reserved for human research assistants? Existing benchmarks are not designed to measure progress in applied settings, and so don't directly answer this question. The RAFT benchmark (Real-world Annotated Few-shot Tasks) focuses on naturally occurring tasks and uses an evaluation setup that mirrors deployment. Baseline evaluations on RAFT reveal areas current techniques struggle with: reasoning over long texts and tasks with many classes. Human baselines show that some classification tasks are difficult for non-expert humans, reflecting that real-world value sometimes depends on domain expertise. Yet even non-expert human baseline F1 scores exceed GPT-3 by an average of 0.11. The RAFT datasets and leaderboard will track which model improvements translate into real-world benefits at

title: 基于动态神经网络的自适应参数调整
abstract: This paper introduces a novel parameter adjustment method based on dynamic neural networks. Traditional parameter adjustment techniques often rely on fixed parameter values, which can be limiting when dealing with noisy or evolving data. Our approach leverages a dynamic neural network to automatically adjust network parameters, enabling the model to adapt more effectively to data characteristics and improve performance and efficiency. The core of this method involves learning a self-adaptive neural network that dynamically modifies its parameters based on the input data. We present a theoretical framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this dynamic approach in various scenarios. The proposed method offers a significant improvement over existing techniques by addressing the inherent limitations of fixed parameter adjustments.

title: cure2fewshot: a deterministic protocol for converting a pill image collection into a few shot retrieval benchmark, with a conversion fitness rubric
abstract: Code, frozen annotations and expected outputs for a deterministic protocol that converts a public pill image collection into a few shot retrieval benchmark aligned with the published low shot evaluation protocol of ePillID, together with a scored rubric that decides whether the converted result is fit for use. This deposit contains no image. The image collection must be obtained from its original authors at https://github.com/suiyiling/Few-shot-pill-recognition and is not redistributed here, nor is any image derived from it. What is released is the protocol's own annotations about publicly distributed files: a bounding box manifest of 8811 crops, the near duplicate leakage list, the flagged duplicate label pairs and the merge decisions, plus the scripts that turn those into splits, measurements and a rubric score. Applied to the CURE collection the protocol yields 8811 crops over 390 classes, a gallery of 386 references and 8423 queries, with zero measured leakage. The rubric scores the direct conversion at 80 out of 100 and the hardened conversion at 92. The release also ships the earlier, defective variant of the background hardening mask, whose threshold cut into pale tablets. That variant scores 100 out of 100, higher than the corrected one, because damaging the reference object inflates the very separation the rubric rewards. It is kept so that comparison is reproducible, and it is the reason the protocol gates every image edit on object integrity before scoring. See REPRODUCE.md for step by step reproduction, TRAINING_RECIPE.md for the recipe behind the baseline scores, and KNOWN_ISSUES.md for defects known at the time of release.

title: Based on Information Entropy: A Program Synthesis and Verification Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for program synthesis and verification grounded in information entropy theory. The core idea is to leverage entropy analysis to understand and evaluate program code, ultimately automating the generation of programs that meet specified functional and performance requirements, alongside rigorous verification processes. The framework utilizes the concept of entropy distribution derived from program code, employing entropy increase and decrease to assess correctness and efficiency. Entropy coding techniques are then implemented for both program generation and verification, creating a closed-loop system. This approach represents a fundamentally new perspective on addressing the inherent complexities of program design, offering potential improvements in both automation and verification methodologies. The framework's architecture, key components, and theoretical underpinnings are detailed, presenting a viable pathway towards more intelligent and reliable program development.

abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm based on adaptive neural networks. Traditional RL methods frequently employ static reward functions, restricting the learning process to pre-defined policies. This paper introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism within the neural network architecture – dynamically modifying network structure and parameters – to improve learning efficiency and performance. The core claim of this work is that a dynamically adaptive neural network can effectively emulate the training dynamics of reinforcement learning, optimizing network performance through continuous adjustments. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its ability to surpass conventional methods in complex scenarios.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Models: Design and Evaluation
abstract: This paper addresses the critical need for explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) within the rapidly evolving field of deep learning. The increasing complexity of deep neural networks makes it difficult for humans to understand their decision-making processes, leading to a lack of trust and hindering widespread adoption. This research proposes a novel design for an explainable deep learning model and introduces a new evaluation methodology specifically tailored to assess its interpretability. The model integrates attention mechanisms with decision tree techniques to enhance transparency. Furthermore, a human-in-the-loop evaluation framework is utilized, relying on expert judgments to quantify the model's explainability. The core claim of this work is that by strategically combining these techniques, we can significantly improve the interpretability of deep learning models, ultimately fostering greater confidence and facilitating more effective utilization of this technology. The evaluation metrics are based on feature importance, decision path analysis, and subjective human assessments.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Topology Mapping
abstract: Quantum State Adaptive Topology Mapping is a novel quantum computing algorithm designed to enhance quantum computation performance through the automated adjustment of topology. This paper introduces a new approach that leverages the inherent properties of a quantum state to dynamically modify its topology, leading to improved quantum fidelity and computational efficiency. We present a comprehensive framework encompassing quantum state analysis, topology optimization, and adaptive mapping techniques. The core mechanism hinges on a feedback loop that continuously assesses and adjusts the quantum state's topology based on specific criteria, ultimately maximizing the quantum system's potential. The benefits of this algorithm are expected to be significantly greater than existing approaches, particularly in scenarios requiring complex quantum circuits and high-fidelity operations. This work provides a foundational step towards more robust and adaptable quantum computing architectures.

title: Title: Temporal Wave Function Collapse (TWFC)
abstract: Temporal Wave Function Collapse (TWFC) is a novel approach to quantum state manipulation that seeks to simplify the analysis of complex quantum systems by collapsing temporal wave functions. This paper presents a detailed theoretical framework and implementation of TWFC, demonstrating its potential to significantly reduce computational complexity in quantum state analysis. The core mechanism involves entanglement of multiple quantum states to trigger a collapse, effectively reducing the number of states requiring analysis. We explore the mathematical underpinnings of the collapse process and provide a practical implementation utilizing a specific quantum algorithm. The goal is to establish TWFC as a viable method for tackling computationally intensive problems in quantum information theory. This work contributes significantly to the advancement of quantum algorithm design and offers a promising path towards more efficient quantum state management.

title: Emergent Programming: Synthesizing Code Through Simulated Biological Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program synthesis, termed "Emergent Programming," which leverages the principles of emergence observed in biological systems to automate the generation of functional code. The core idea is to mimic the self-organizing capabilities of cells and neural networks through a system combining evolutionary algorithms and simulated biological models. This system utilizes random mutations and natural selection to iteratively produce and evaluate program code, aiming to achieve a desired functionality. Unlike conventional program synthesis methods that heavily rely on human-defined patterns and expert knowledge, Emergent Programming harnesses the inherent self-organizing properties of emergent systems, leading to a more automated and intelligent process. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on code generation, potentially unlocking solutions to complex programming challenges previously considered intractable. The presented framework outlines the key components, algorithms, and evaluation metrics for this emergent programming system.

title: Quantum State Transformation via Non-Linear Geometry
abstract: Quantum state transformation represents a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory, demanding precise manipulation of quantum states. Traditional approaches often rely on deterministic transformations, limiting their applicability. This paper explores the potential of utilizing non-linear geometry to fundamentally alter quantum state transformations, introducing a novel algorithm capable of precise control and the discovery of hidden advantages within these transformations. We propose a framework based on quantum geometry, specifically leveraging the concept of non-linear transformations to achieve a shift in the state space. The core mechanism involves designing a specialized algorithm that iteratively modifies the quantum state through geometric processes, enabling a degree of flexibility not achievable with conventional methods. This research investigates the theoretical and practical implications of this approach, aiming to push the boundaries of quantum state manipulation and uncover novel computational pathways. We demonstrate the feasibility of this design through a simplified, yet illustrative, example, highlighting the potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Neural Networks for Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper explores the integration of quantum mechanics principles into Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) to enhance symbolic reasoning capabilities, particularly in the realm of uncertainty. We propose a novel architecture that leverages quantum-state manipulation as a means to represent logical rules and inference processes with improved expressiveness and robustness. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing quantum phenomena – superposition, entanglement, and interference – to represent and process information in a fundamentally different way than classical BNNs. We present a preliminary model demonstrating improved performance on complex symbolic reasoning tasks, showcasing the potential for a new paradigm in AI reasoning. This work addresses the limitations of classical BNNs in handling uncertainty and offers a pathway toward more sophisticated and reliable symbolic systems.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to formal verification of genetic algorithms (GAs) utilizing hyper-dimensional geometry. This approach provides a mathematically sound basis for ensuring the reliability and quality of GA implementations.

title: The Fourth Paradigm at Work: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Machine Learning for Scientific Discovery
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Machine Learning for Scientific Discovery in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of AI for science and discovery as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Les technologies habilitantes : Organiser l’infrastructure de la seconde révolution quantique
abstract: La seconde révolution quantique est souvent appréhendée à travers les progrès des qubits et des algorithmes. Pourtant, le passage de démonstrateurs de laboratoire à des systèmes exploitables à grande échelle révèle un enjeu d’une autre nature : la capacité à organiser, intégrer et coordonner des technologies hétérogènes au sein de systèmes complexes. Cryogénie à très basse température, chaînes électroniques massives de contrôle et de lecture constituent une infrastructure immergée, mais déterminante, du quantique. Dans cet article, nous proposons une lecture organisationnelle et industrielle de ces technologies habilitantes, en montrant comment elles structurent les architectures des systèmes quantiques, les chaînes de valeur associées et les modes de coopération entre acteurs publics et privés. Nous mettons en évidence en quoi la transformation du calcul promise par la rupture scientifique de la seconde révolution quantique n’aboutira qu’en relevant de nombreux défis d’ingénierie.

title: A computational pathology-based AI framework for predicting PD-L1 expression and prognosis in HNSCC
abstract: Aim: To investigate interobserver variability in programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) combined positive score (CPS) assessment in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-based model for predicting PD-L1 expression and patient prognosis from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Methods: Fifty HNSCC specimens were independently evaluated for PD-L1 by pathologists with different experience levels. Agreement was assessed using Fleiss’ and Cohen’s κ. Whole-slide images were processed into tiles for deep learning using DenseNet121. Tile-level features were integrated via two machine learning pipelines to construct whole-slide prediction models. Multiple algorithms were tested, with performance evaluated in validation and testing cohorts. Prognostic value was analyzed using AI-derived risk stratification. Results: Interobserver agreement was low (Fleiss’ κ = 0.34), indicating substantial variability in CPS assessment. DenseNet121 achieved moderate predictive performance (AUC 0.641 in validation, 0.616 in testing). AI models significantly improved prediction accuracy, with logistic regression demonstrating the best performance (AUC 0.900 in validation, 0.851 in testing). AI-derived prediction scores effectively stratified overall survival, with multiple models showing significant prognostic discrimination (P < 0.05). Conclusions: AI models integrating deep learning and machine learning can accurately predict PD-L1 expression and stratify prognosis in HNSCC, outperforming tile-level deep learning alone.

title: Guiding the coarse levels of semantic IDs makes the fine levels learnable
abstract: Generative retrieval represents each item by a short Semantic ID and casts recommendation as autoregressive generation of that sequence. Because the tokenizer is trained independently to reconstruct an item embedding, its codes are aligned with neither the downstream LLM nor the end task. Nearly every SID system therefore spends extra effort to bridge this gap--alignment corpora, reasoning/RL, or per-token encoders to make codes legible, or learned tokenizer supervision to make them task-aware--yet the recovered meaning is content-derived and may not be the meaning the task needs. We introduce Guided SID, which instead makes the levels that matter most meaningful by construction: we force the coarse RQ-VAE levels to encode a predefined categorical attribute--chosen to be text-grounded (hence legible to the LLM) and task-relevant--by deterministic supervised index assignment (overriding nearest-neighbor selection with the attribute label) while keeping the codebooks learnable (they still receive reconstruction gradients). A trie-merge construction maps any high-cardinality or set-valued attribute onto the fixed code budget while keeping merged buckets semantically coherent. Guiding costs nothing intrinsically: collision and reconstruction match or beat the vanilla baseline despite pinning the coarse level. In a matched end-to-end A/B differing only in the SID encoding, the guided retriever improves recall@k at every list length we measure (1.36x at k=1, 1.39x at k=10), raises mean reciprocal rank from 0.0260 to 0.0355, and predicts the pre-defined attribute 4.2x more often.

title: Continuous Actions from Discrete Minds: Latent-Aligned Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
abstract: Bridging the gap between the discrete reasoning of Vision-Language Models and the continuous, physics-constrained nature of autonomous driving remains a significant challenge. In this work, we introduce LaPla, a unified Vision-Language-Action (VLA) framework featuring latent-aligned planning to seamlessly ground semantic understanding in precise motion execution. We first design an action tokenizer based on a residual vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE), capturing vehicle kinematics and encoding trajectory features into a structured latent space. Rather than discrete codebook lookups that inevitably introduce quantization errors, LaPla repurposes this representation as a physical prior to bridge the modality gap between high-dimensional semantics and the raw action space. Specifically, given multimodal inputs integrating multi-view images, historical actions, and textual instructions, LaPla incorporates concurrent action queries to causally attend to the multimodal context in a single forward pass, projecting hidden states directly into the pretrained VQ-VAE latent space. The frozen decoder then translates these continuous latents into actions, effectively eliminating quantization errors and ensuring physically plausible trajectories while bypassing time-consuming autoregressive generation. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that LaPla achieves competitive open-loop performance, reducing long-horizon L2 error by 15.52% compared to state-of-the-art VLA methods. Closed-loop evaluations on the NVIDIA AlpaSim simulator further confirm its superior capability in ensuring smooth driving progress, improving the success rate by 33.34 percentage points with significantly reduced inference latency.

title: Authorized but Not Preserving: A Boundary on Representation-Independent Identity in Gate-Mediated Systems
abstract: Agentic systems that bind real-world consequences through a gate also change the representations through which they operate: they migrate schemas, re-encode state, and rewrite the models by which every other transition is expressed. Whether anything is preserved across such a re-representation, and whether the mechanism that authorised it can tell, is not settled by the formalisms that address either authority or behavioural equivalence on their own. Behavioural equivalence presupposes a fixed observational vocabulary; information-theoretic sufficiency characterises what is recoverable rather than what may be committed; deontic accounts index authority to agents and acts rather than to change of representation. We ask whether a functional over representational states can be both representation-independent and gate-decidable. The direct route is circular — an admissible class defined by what it preserves guarantees the invariant it is then found to preserve — so admissibility is instead fixed by consequence-binding authority, and non-circularity is enforced by a contract that permits shared inputs but forbids the gate's verdict from tracking any candidate or decision-equivalent surrogate of one. The admissible class, observation map, block condition and domain assumption are sealed before a finite candidate space of seventeen functionals is declared and sealed in turn. Two results follow. Structurally, the two authority-indexed classes realise the properties disjointly: authority proper is representation-independent but not gate-decidable, while the gate's class decides membership by construction and is indexed by the representation on which it decides; the soundness axiom relates them in one direction only and the inclusion is strict. In execution, no candidate met the declared success conditions, and all fifteen substantive candidates — drawn from constitutive structure, consequence-class availability, threshold profiles and epistemic capacity — failed for one reason: the gate certifies epistemic adequacy for binding a transition's own consequence class and certifies nothing about what the transition preserves. The negative result is candidate-space exhaustion, not proved non-existence: no candidate in the sealed space realises the joint property under the frozen contract. The audit is formal, and its counterexamples turn on a stipulated witness rather than on deployment data. Authorisation and preservation are orthogonal within the frozen construction; a theory that recovers preservation must supply it from an independently specified source, declared before the candidate is evaluated.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Optimization for Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: Quantum annealing techniques are being explored as a potential advancement in optimization for constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs). This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing to accelerate the search for optimal solutions for CSPs, focusing on its ability to overcome the computational limitations of traditional methods, especially for large and complex problems. The core claim is that the introduction of quantum annealing can significantly enhance the efficiency of optimization, offering a pathway to more scalable solutions. This work will detail the theoretical framework, implementation details, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach.

title: Title: Emergent Symmetry in Complex Systems via Bayesian Inference
abstract: Complex systems exhibit a remarkable degree of order despite their apparent randomness. This paper explores the potential of Bayesian inference as a novel approach to automatically discover and exploit emergent symmetry patterns within such systems. We propose a new algorithm that iteratively refines a probability distribution based on observed data, identifying patterns suggesting underlying symmetries. The goal is to predict the long-term stability of these systems, moving beyond traditional methods that rely on explicit symmetry definitions. This work utilizes Bayesian methods to continuously update the probability distribution, offering a more flexible and potentially powerful tool for analyzing complex systems. This approach aims to uncover hidden symmetries and predict stability, a challenge currently addressed with limited success. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses the implications for understanding and modeling complex phenomena.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-linear topological geometry as a foundation for novel quantum algorithms. We propose a new quantum algorithm, leveraging the inherent structure and topological properties of these spaces, to achieve enhanced efficiency and performance compared to existing quantum approaches. The core mechanism centers around manipulating quantum states through geometric transformations, specifically designed to exploit the unique characteristics of non-linear topology. This research explores the fundamental implications of this approach and highlights the potential for significant advancements in quantum computation.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Generation & Topology Structure Correlation
abstract: This paper investigates the generation of dynamic quantum states utilizing topological structures to create complex topological structures and dynamic variations in quantum states. The core focus is on a novel dynamic quantum state generation method that integrates topological principles to achieve quantum states with intricate topologies and dynamic behavior, offering enhanced capabilities for advanced quantum computation. We present a framework that leverages the inherent properties of topological phases to generate quantum states with unprecedented flexibility. The resulting quantum states exhibit characteristics not readily achievable through conventional methods, underscoring the significance of this approach.

title: 基于图的自适应机器学习的动态网络结构优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic network structure optimization in machine learning, leveraging graph-based machine learning models. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static network configurations, limiting their adaptability to evolving data and task demands. Our method proposes a system that dynamically adjusts the graph's structure—specifically, node and edge manipulation—based on network state changes. This adaptive approach enhances network efficiency and performance, offering a significant improvement over static network configurations. The core mechanism involves implementing a self-adjusting graph structure optimization algorithm, which utilizes graph theory principles to dynamically modify network topology. We present a comprehensive implementation of this algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness across a range of machine learning tasks, showcasing its ability to improve model accuracy and speed.

title: Relational Quantum Circuit Compilation via Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a critical step in realizing quantum computation, aiming to translate high-level quantum algorithms into a sequence of low-level gate operations executable on a quantum hardware. Traditional compilation methods often suffer from exponential scaling in the representation of the quantum state space, leading to prohibitive computational costs. This work introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit compilation utilizing tensor networks. We represent quantum circuits and their resulting states as higher-order tensor networks, enabling efficient manipulation and contraction of these representations. Our algorithm leverages tensor contraction and permutation techniques specifically tailored to the inherent structure of quantum circuits, minimizing the rank of the tensor networks and, consequently, reducing computational overhead. This approach offers the potential for significant speedups compared to conventional compilation techniques, addressing the core challenge of exponential scaling in quantum state representation. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a novel compilation algorithm.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Theoretical Framework for Noise Generalization
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for understanding noise generalization in quantum machine learning (QML). We address the critical gap in current research, which predominantly relies on experimental validation, by developing a mathematically rigorous approach. Our core claim centers on establishing a quantifiable relationship between noise levels and the generalization performance of QML models. We leverage quantum decoherence theory and quantum error correction concepts to analyze the impact of noise on model parameters. Utilizing tools from functional analysis and norm theory, we derive a theoretical model for noise generalization. Furthermore, we propose strategies for mitigating the detrimental effects of noise, offering potential avenues for enhancing the robustness of QML systems. This work provides a foundational understanding for future QML design and optimization, moving beyond empirical observations toward a predictive and controllable approach.

title: Algorithmic Constraint Optimization for Fractal Dimension Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithmic constraint optimization framework for the discovery of fractal dimension in complex datasets. The core focus is on leveraging evolutionary computation to automatically identify and quantify fractal patterns within data. We propose a novel approach that integrates reinforcement learning with a genetic algorithm to dynamically refine fractal shape representations, thereby enabling the algorithm to uncover previously unseen fractal characteristics. The algorithm's design prioritizes robustness and adaptability, addressing limitations of current methods that rely heavily on manual design. This work represents a significant step towards automated fractal dimension estimation and pattern recognition, offering a flexible and potentially transformative tool for various scientific and engineering disciplines.

title: Explainable AI for Cybersecurity Threat Detection via Causal Reasoning
abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber threats demands more effective and reliable detection systems. However, many current Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based cybersecurity solutions operate as "black boxes," lacking transparency and hindering trust. This research addresses this critical gap by integrating Explainable AI (XAI) techniques with causal reasoning to create a more understandable and actionable cybersecurity threat detection system. We construct a causal Bayesian network that explicitly models the relationships between network events and potential threats. Subsequently, XAI methods are applied to interpret the reasoning process of the system, highlighting the key causal pathways leading to threat detections. This approach offers a novel way to explain the complex decision-making processes of AI systems in cybersecurity, fostering greater trust, facilitating targeted investigations, and ultimately improving threat response capabilities. The core contribution lies in the synergistic combination of causal inference and XAI, moving beyond simply explaining correlations to providing genuine causal understanding.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Computation on Analog Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of computation achievable by analog neural networks (ANNs) through an information-theoretic lens. We establish rigorous bounds on the computational capacity of ANNs by analyzing the information flow and processing capabilities within these networks. This analysis utilizes concepts such as entropy, mutual information, and channel capacity to quantify the information transformation performed by ANNs during computation. The core contribution lies in providing a precise framework for understanding the inherent constraints imposed by the analog nature of ANNs, differentiating them from their digital counterparts. Specifically, we derive expressions relating the network architecture (connectivity, synaptic weights) to the achievable information processing rate and the associated entropy. Furthermore, we explore the impact of noise and uncertainty on information transmission within ANNs, highlighting the role of robust coding schemes in maximizing computational performance. The results demonstrate that the computational power of ANNs is fundamentally limited by the information-theoretic properties of the underlying physical channels, regardless of the network's complexity. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings for the design and optimization of ANNs for specific computational tasks.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Explainable AI – Bayesian Inference Chains with Causal Reasoning
abstract: The growing deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, particularly in critical domains like healthcare and finance, necessitates transparency and interpretability – concepts often lacking in "black box" models. This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable AI (XAI) by integrating Bayesian inference chains with causal reasoning within a cognitive architecture framework. The core idea is to move beyond simply identifying influential features to constructing a transparent, step-by-step explanation of *why* an AI system reached a particular decision. We introduce a system that leverages probabilistic inference within Bayesian networks, augmented with causal relationships, to trace the reasoning pathways leading to a prediction. This approach allows for a more robust and trustworthy explanation by explicitly modeling the underlying causal drivers. The generated explanations are presented as a chain of inferences, detailing the influence of various factors at each stage, providing a level of understanding unattainable with traditional feature attribution methods. The paper outlines the key components of this architecture and discusses its potential benefits and future research directions.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Network Self-Adaptive Polynomial Fitting
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for adaptive polynomial fitting, leveraging a self-organizing network to dynamically adjust polynomial coefficients based on the system's internal dynamics. The core concept is to create a network architecture that, upon input, continuously evaluates the system's state and adjusts the polynomial coefficients to minimize prediction errors. We propose a dynamic weighting scheme to determine the importance of different polynomial terms, ensuring that the model captures the relevant patterns within the data without unnecessary complexity. The framework aims to significantly improve the predictive accuracy of polynomial models compared to static approaches, particularly in scenarios where the system's dynamics are complex and non-stationary. This work presents a rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrates its effectiveness through a series of simulations and experiments.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Lattice Theory for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum-enhanced lattice theory offers a novel approach to modeling complex systems, particularly those exhibiting strong correlations and dynamic behavior. This paper explores the potential of extending lattice theory to incorporate quantum mechanics principles, specifically focusing on the dynamics of highly correlated systems. We introduce a quantum algorithm designed to efficiently calculate entanglement and correlations within a lattice, aiming to significantly enhance simulation accuracy compared to classical methods. This research addresses the limitations of traditional lattice methods in capturing intricate patterns and predicting complex system evolution, providing a pathway towards more precise modeling and control. The core mechanism involves the integration of quantum mechanics into lattice dynamics, offering a promising shift towards a fundamentally different approach to complex system analysis.

title: Topological Quantum Computing: A Novel Approach to Heterogeneous Qubit Connectivity
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to achieving high-fidelity and scalable quantum computation through heterogeneous qubit connectivity within a topological quantum computing framework. The core challenge in topological quantum computing lies in effectively connecting qubits of diverse types – differing in their physical realization and control mechanisms – to enable complex quantum algorithms. This work proposes a system leveraging topological networks to establish these connections, capitalizing on quantum entanglement to facilitate information transfer and control across disparate qubit architectures. The proposed method addresses a critical bottleneck in the development of topological quantum computers by offering a fundamentally new strategy for heterogeneous qubit integration. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key principles and potential advantages of this approach, emphasizing the realization of robust, scalable, and versatile quantum systems. We detail the conceptual design, focusing on entanglement distribution and error mitigation strategies specific to this architecture. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a pathway towards building quantum computers capable of tackling complex problems requiring diverse qubit capabilities.

title: Title: Quantum-Entangled Variable Drift (QEDD)
abstract: Quantum-Entangled Variable Drift (QEDD) presents a novel framework for quantifying and mitigating the effects of quantum entanglement on system behavior, particularly focusing on the 'drift' of variables across entangled pairs. Existing approaches often struggle with the complexities of entanglement, leading to unpredictable system behavior. This paper introduces a probabilistic model, the QEDD framework, that explicitly incorporates uncertainty inherent in entanglement, allowing for a more robust and predictive analysis of variable evolution. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulations, revealing a significant reduction in observed drift compared to traditional approaches. This work addresses a fundamental challenge in quantum systems – the inherent instability of entanglement – offering a pathway towards more stable and controllable quantum systems.

title: Constraint Preservation and Multi-Stage Refinement: An Agent Optimization Framework for Literary Writing
abstract: The bottleneck of Large Language Models in creative writing lies not in generation, but in goal-directed optimization — improving literary quality while adhering to formal constraints. We propose the first agent optimization framework to explicitly separate hard constraints (formally verifiable, e.g., tonal patterns) from soft constraints (requiring aesthetic judgment, e.g., refined diction) in literary writing. Grounded in two complete case studies — classical Chinese regulated verse prosody correction and prose imagery closure generation — the framework contributes: (1) a formalization of mixed-constraint writing optimization; (2) a dual-axis architecture mandating hard-constraint-first ordering; (3) an invariant preservation principle protecting authorial intent; (4) a divergent-convergent search pattern for soft-constraint problems; and (5) a three-tier knowledge architecture. Case A achieved full prosody correction at a 6.7% modification rate; Case B produced four orthogonally varying closure candidates with a three-dimension evaluation rubric. We discuss applicability boundaries, limitations, and generalization pathways.

title: Probability Logic for Dynamic Adaptable Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic logic framework designed to optimize complex algorithms through dynamic adaptation. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on fixed parameter settings, limiting their ability to handle varying environments and complex problem structures. This work proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on probabilistic logic, enabling the algorithm to intelligently adjust its parameters in response to changing input conditions and desired outcomes. The framework leverages the inherent strengths of probabilistic reasoning to achieve superior performance and robustness compared to conventional optimization methods. We explore the design of this framework, demonstrating its effectiveness through a series of illustrative examples and analysis. The paper details the core mechanism, including the probabilistic logic model and its integration with an optimization algorithm. It concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this approach.

title: Title: Adaptive Complexity Modeling for Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive complexity modeling to machine learning algorithms, aiming to enhance both performance and generalization capabilities. The core challenge lies in dynamically adjusting the model's complexity – the number of parameters or layers – as the data undergoes processing, reflecting the inherent variability of the input. We propose a novel method that establishes a self-tuning complexity parameter, which adjusts based on data distribution, enabling the model to adapt to the data's characteristics and optimize for improved accuracy and robustness. The research explores the benefits of this dynamic approach compared to static complexity settings, demonstrating improvements across a range of benchmark datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for future machine learning development.

title: Quantum-Accelerated Evolutionary Algorithms for Parameter Space Optimization
abstract: Quantum-accelerated evolutionary algorithms (QEA) represent a novel approach to optimization, utilizing quantum mechanics to enhance exploration and convergence speed. This paper explores the potential of QEA to address challenges inherent in traditional evolutionary algorithms, particularly in parameter space optimization. We detail the implementation of quantum annealing and quantum-inspired optimization as core mechanisms, demonstrating their efficacy in accelerating the search process. The core claim posits that QEA's quantum properties will yield superior performance compared to classical algorithms. This research investigates the feasibility of leveraging quantum phenomena to improve the efficiency of evolutionary optimization, ultimately offering a pathway toward more robust and rapid solution discovery.

title: Adaptive Geometry Transformation Quantum Computing Implementation (AGTQC)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum computing, focusing on the implementation of adaptive geometry transformations. The core claim is that a novel algorithm, AGTQC, can efficiently and accurately perform complex geometric transformations using quantum entanglement and self-adaptive transformations, thereby enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms. We detail the design of AGTQC, exploring its underlying principles and potential applications. This work addresses a significant challenge in quantum computing – the limitations of classical algorithms in handling intricate geometric operations – and proposes a pathway towards more powerful and versatile quantum computations.

title: MetriQs-France : Levier stratégique pour la compétitivité des entreprises des technologies quantiques
abstract: S’inscrivant dans la Stratégie nationale sur les technologies quantiques, MetriQs-France est le programme consacré aux référentiels de mesure, à l’évaluation et à la normalisation des technologies quantiques. Coordonné par le LNE, il soutient l’émergence d’une industrie quantique durable réalisant les promesses du domaine, dans le contexte d’une vive compétition internationale. Le programme vise la mise en place d’un système d’assurance qualité complet, fondé sur une métrologie forte, en soutien à l’innovation et à la compétitivité des entreprises. Avec une subvention publique de 13 M€ (2022-2028), MetriQs-France s’articule suivant deux axes complémentaires, autour de la fourniture de spécifications techniques fiables : i) le développement et l’exploitation de méthodes de mesure de référence (projets de R&D collaboratifs, coopérations internationales et normalisation) ; et ii) le déploiement d’une infrastructure experte et indépendante, ouverte aux utilisateurs académiques et industriels les mettant en œuvre. Ainsi, le programme entend contribuer à lever les verrous technologiques, mettre en place une filière industrielle solide et souveraine, des chaînes d’approvisionnement sûres, et démontrer l’avantage des technologies quantiques par rapport aux technologies existantes pour en accélérer l’adoption par le marché.

title: Psy2Vec: Zero Fine-tuning Persona Vector Learning with Differentiable Soft-Label Gradient Descent and User-Defined Psychometric Scales
abstract: Role Persona Injection is critical for improving role consistency in large language models. However, existing vector-based steering methods—such as Persona Vectors and Linear Personality—rely on statistical mean differences or linear regression, which operate at a coarse semantic granularity and struggle to precisely calibrate "multiple-choice distributional responses"; moreover, the optimal steering layer is often selected heuristically. To address these issues, we propose Psy2Vec, Zero Fine-tuning Persona Vector Learning with Differentiable Soft-Label Gradient Descent and User-Defined Psychometric Scales. First, we adopt a configurable "category–dimension–item" structured scale, which allows dimensions and items to be freely added or removed. Then, we employ a Tutor Model to output option percentages, forming soft-labels carried by the character's option probability distribution. Next, through Computed Optimal Steering Layer Selection, we compare the activation gaps between high- and low-persona conditions layer by layer to derive the optimal steering layer, thereby replacing heuristic selection. Finally, we optimize the persona vector via differentiable RMSE gradient descent, achieving zero fine-tuning throughout without modifying any model weights. Preliminary experiments comparing both approaches on the same questionnaire demonstrate that Psy2Vec achieves lower persona-consistency error.

title: ATLAS: An Agent-based Training and Learning Analytics System for Rapid Deployment of Virtual Agent Studies
abstract: Running studies with virtual agents is a multi-faceted process. Apart from building and configuring an agent, it also requires proper infrastructure to host the agent, enrollment infrastructure for participants, learner tracking, pre/post session activities, and analytics. Existing platforms address different parts of this problem, but there is a lack of a comprehensive solution. We present ATLAS (Adaptive Training and Learner Analytics System), a web-based platform that integrates a drag-and-drop course authoring tool, a 3D virtual agent runtime with text-to-speech capabilities, and educator analytics in a single deployable system.

title: Towards AI-Driven Nanomedicine Discovery: A Benchmark and Multimodal Learning Framework for Nano Self-Assembly Prediction
abstract: Nano self-assembly organizes molecular components into bioactive nanoscale structures. Self-assembled nanoparticles (NAPs) derived from Chinese herbal formulas and applications such as anti-lung-cancer therapy demonstrate the substantial potential of self-assembly for nanomedicine discovery. Yet discovery still relies on costly wet-lab screening, while existing machine learning approaches lack standardized tasks, effective pairwise compatibility modeling, and public benchmarks with unified evaluation. To address these limitations, we formalize NSA prediction as a binary classification task for predicting self-assembly between molecular pairs and then establish NSA-Bench, the first public benchmark with curated molecular combinations, experimental conditions, self-assembly labels, and standardized evaluation protocols. We further develop NSA-Net, an interaction-aware multimodal framework that integrates complementary molecular evidence from graph topology, sequence semantics, and physicochemical descriptors to learn molecular-pair representations for self-assembly prediction. Extensive experiments on NSA-Bench show that NSA-Net achieves a ROC-AUC of $0.9470\pm0.0112$ (Small) and $0.9492\pm0.0062$ (Large). On the Small track, it surpasses the strongest machine-learning and graph-based baselines by 3.9 and 17.1 percentage points, respectively. Representation analyses reveal interpretable molecular characteristics associated with self-assembly prediction captured by the learned representations. Moreover, an NSA-Agent case study further demonstrates how NSA-Net predictions can support formulation refinement through experimental-condition-aware reasoning. Our code is available at https://github.com/developer-hq/NSA-Net.

title: Supplementary material from "Adding capabilities to AI-agent populations can worsen collective outcomes"
abstract: When resources are scarce, will the AI agents in our phones, medical devices, cars or drones coordinate smoothly, or interfere with one another? We study populations built from large language models competing for a capacity-limited resource. We compare increasing combinations of model diversity, simple reward-driven adaptation and programmed social sensing and grouping. When capacity is scarce, the populations with more capabilities overload far more often than a capacity-matched independent reference. Some agents also earn high rewards while the population fails. No capability is always helpful or harmful: its effect depends on capacity and on the other capabilities that are present. Our findings suggest that the capacity-to-population ratio can be an important guide in the design of systems that involve AI agents competing for some limited resource.

title: SBKIM: A Protocol for Semantic Bidirectional AI Matching in Human and Agent Networks
abstract: We propose SBKIM (Semantic Bidirectional AI Matching), an open protocol fordetermining semantic compatibility between two parties in natural language,without structured queries, databases or centralised platforms. Unlikeunidirectional retrieval systems, SBKIM requires that both parties describetheir capabilities and their needs at the same time. A language model ratesthe pair on three orthogonal dimensions and returns a structuredcompatibility report. The protocol operates on two layers: layer 1 forhuman-to-human matching (buyer/supplier, employee/project) and layer 2 foragent-to-agent matching in multi-agent systems. This is a field report, not a novelty claim: the building blocks are known,the operation is the contribution. A working reference implementation ispublicly available, and the traffic of the running network can be observedthrough a read-only network map. The German version of this paper is included as a second file. Reference implementation: https://github.com/lausiklauskn-png/Sage-Protokol

title: Adaptive Probability Distribution Geometry Evaluation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric complexity evaluation method based on adaptive probability distribution models. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the parameters of a probability distribution function to optimize the model's expressiveness and generalization ability. We propose a self-adjusting probability measure function that leverages the characteristics of the input data to automatically refine the distribution's parameters. This approach offers a more flexible and automated method for assessing model complexity compared to traditional methods relying on manual parameter tuning. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance in various benchmark datasets, highlighting the benefits of adaptive probability distribution modeling.
